summary: Adelanto sprawls across nearly 53 square miles of high desert floor north of the Cajon Pass, which means its population density — about 690 people per square mile — is closer to a rural township than a suburb, and the landscape reflects it: long stretches of creosote scrub, Joshua trees at the periphery, and unobstructed sightlines toward the San Gabriel and San Bernardino Mountains that make sunsets genuinely dramatic. With a median home price around $318,300 against a median household income of roughly $68,400, the price-to-income ratio sits near 4.7 — significantly more accessible than most of Southern California, though that math shifts when you factor in the commute reality: Adelanto functions largely as a bedroom community, with many workers driving south through the Cajon Pass toward San Bernardino or the Inland Empire, a corridor notorious for traffic bottlenecks. The local employment base leans on logistics, correctional facilities, and municipal services rather than a broad private-sector mix, so switching jobs without switching cities is genuinely constrained. The city averages nearly 11 hours of sunshine daily and highs around 76°F year-round, but summer peaks in the Victor Valley regularly push past 100°F, and winter nights drop into the 30s — a desert swing that shapes daily routines. Adelanto is, at its core, an affordable square footage play whose price tag is inseparable from its isolation.
